{{Quote|I am remembering something I accessed earlier. The chief designer of the Ma'aood funerary temples directed his draftsmen that all obvious passages should be booby-trapped, and all traps should be made as inviting as possible.|Lobot|<ref name="Shield of Lies">''[[Shield of Lies]]''</ref>}}
The '''Ma'aood''' were a group beings known for the wondrous temples they built and protected with traps.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|272|Ma'aood}}</ref> The [[Ma'aood chief designer|chief designer]] of the [[Ma'aood funerary temple]]s ensured that all the obvious passages were filled with traps that appeared as inviting as possible to beings that entered the temples.<ref name="Shield of Lies" /> By around [[16 ABY/Legends|16 ABY]],<ref name="Shield of Lies Date">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[The Black Fleet Crisis]]'' series to between [[16 ABY/Legends|16 ABY]] and [[17 ABY/Legends|17 ABY]], thus [[Lobot/Legends|Lobot]] must have had knowledge of the Ma'aood by around that [[Standard year/Legends|year]].</ref> [[Lobot/Legends|Lobot]], a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]], was familiar with the chief designer directive to install traps in the Ma'aood temples.<ref name="Shield of Lies" /> Around that [[Standard year/Legends|year]], while exploring the organic starship ''[[Teljkon Vagabond]]'', Lobot recounted the fact to his friend [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]].<ref name="Shield of Lies" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Ma'aood were first mentioned in ''[[Shield of Lies]]'', the second novel in ''[[The Black Fleet Crisis]]'' series. The novel was written by [[Michael P. Kube-McDowell]] and released in [[1996]].<ref name="Shield of Lies" /> Mention of the Ma'aood was not included in the novel's [[Shield of Lies (abridged audiobook)|abridged audiobook]] released alongside the book.<ref name="Abridged Audiobook">[[Shield of Lies (abridged audiobook)|''Shield of Lies'' abridged audiobook]]</ref>
